# Move an app to the Material 3 defaults

From this release the JSKIT web packages draw exact Material 3 themselves, in
light and dark, on phone, tablet and desktop: the shell, its app bar and
navigation, list-detail pages and the CRUD list, view, new and edit screens.
An app needs no CSS, overrides or patches of its own to look right, so moving
an existing app is mostly deleting. [Material 3](../framework/material-3.md)
describes the result; this page lists what changes in an app's source.

Upgrade the JSKIT packages together first ([Upgrade JSKIT](./upgrading-jskit.md)),
then work through the sections below. Nothing here changes a feature, field,
action, permission or validation.

## 1. Theme: one seed, from `@jskit-ai/material-web`

Add `@jskit-ai/material-web` to the app's dependencies and build Vuetify from
it in `src/main.js`:

```js
import "vuetify/styles";
import "@jskit-ai/material-web/client/material.css";
import { createVuetify } from "vuetify";
import * as components from "vuetify/components";
import * as directives from "vuetify/directives";
import { createMaterialVuetifyOptions } from "@jskit-ai/material-web/client";
import { theme } from "./theme/index.js";

const vuetify = createVuetify({ components, directives, ...createMaterialVuetifyOptions(theme) });
```

`src/theme/index.js` holds the app's only theme facts:

```js
export const theme = {
  seed: "#6750A4",
  colors: {},
  icons: {}
};
```

- Delete hand-written `themes: { light: {...}, dark: {...} }` blocks and every
  hand-picked hex colour. Both schemes come from `seed`, with every Material 3
  role (`primary-container`, `surface-container-high`, `outline-variant`, ...)
  as a theme colour.
- A colour the app really owns (a partner brand, a status of its own) goes in
  `colors` by camelCase name, such as `partner: "#0A7D3E"`. It becomes
  `partner`, `on-partner`, `partner-container` and `on-partner-container`,
  harmonized to the seed, in both schemes; `{ value: "#F5C518", blend: false }`
  keeps a brand colour's own hue. `success`, `warning` and `info` are already
  there.
- Delete `defaultTheme: "light"`. The app now follows the device's light or
  dark setting.

## 2. Delete the app's chrome CSS

Delete, rather than port:

- rules that restyle the shell's app bar, drawer, rail, navigation bar or page
  title, and every `--shell-*` and `--shell-chrome-*` custom property (the shell
  no longer reads them);
- `v-sheet border` panels and outlined cards used as page sections: Material 3
  cards are elevated (`v-card`, the default) or filled
  (`variant="flat" color="surface-container-highest"`), and a section on the
  page needs no frame at all;
- `!important`, Sass variable overrides and component size or radius tweaks.
  `material.css` sets 40dp buttons with a 48dp touch target, 12dp cards, 28dp
  dialogs and sheets, 8dp chips and 16dp FABs, and an app's own props still win;
- every `height` and `min-height` on a button, as a prop, a style or CSS. A
  button that should look smaller becomes `size="small"` or `size="x-small"`:
  it keeps the 48dp touch target. A long label ends in an ellipsis instead of
  spilling out; give a label that can run long its `title`.

Use colour roles (`color="secondary-container"`, `bg-color="surface-container-high"`,
the `on-surface-variant` class) instead of colours.

## 3. Icons: `$aliases`, not `mdi-*`

Replace `mdi-*` strings and `@mdi/js` imports with Vuetify aliases, which are
Material Symbols Rounded glyphs named in camelCase: `mdi-pencil` becomes
`$edit`, `mdi-delete` `$delete`, `mdi-cog-outline` `$settings`,
`mdi-account-circle` `$accountCircle`, `mdi-alert-circle` `$error`,
`mdi-dots-vertical` `$moreVert`. Then remove `@mdi/js` from `package.json`.
The full list is `@jskit-ai/material-web/client/symbols`; a glyph JSKIT lacks
goes in `theme.icons` as its 24x24 path data and works as `$name` everywhere.

## 4. Typography: Material 3 type classes

Vuetify 4 has no Material 2 type classes, so text using them is unstyled.
Rename them:

| Material 2 class | Material 3 class |
| --- | --- |
| `text-h1`, `text-h2`, `text-h3` | `text-display-large`, `text-display-medium`, `text-display-small` |
| `text-h4`, `text-h5`, `text-h6` | `text-headline-large`, `text-headline-small`, `text-title-large` |
| `text-subtitle-1`, `text-subtitle-2` | `text-title-medium`, `text-title-small` |
| `text-body-1`, `text-body-2`, `text-caption` | `text-body-large`, `text-body-medium`, `text-body-small` |
| `text-button`, `text-overline` | `text-label-large`, `text-label-small` |
| `text-medium-emphasis` | `on-surface-variant` |

An app with its own fonts names them in the theme instead of in CSS, so they
keep the app's look: `typography: { brand: '"Fraunces", serif', plain:
'"Inter", sans-serif' }` in `src/theme/index.js` (both Roboto Flex when left
out). `brand` is display, headline and title-large; `plain` is the rest. Delete
the app's `font-family` and `--v-font-body` rules; the app still loads its
font files.

## 5. Pages: titles, parents and the Up arrow

Each page declares its app bar title, and each inner page the page it belongs
to, in its `definePage()` block:

```js
definePage({ meta: { jskit: { title: "Edit book", parent: "/books/:bookId" } } });
```

`parent` is a path on the page's own surface, or `{ surface, path }` for
another one; its `:param` segments take the current route's values. A main
navigation destination declares no parent and shows no arrow. A page with a
parent renders in its surface's shell layout (`ShellLayout` around
`<RouterView />`), which draws the bar with its title, Up and actions:
`jskit check` reports `nav/missing-shell-layout` until it does. Declare
`jskit.surface` only on that layout page: a parent beside it is never read, so
`nav/surface-parent` reports a page that repeats its surface. The account
settings page needs `src/pages/account.vue` from the users/account-settings
pattern. The shell's Up arrow returns to the page the person came from, or else
to the parent, so:

- delete "Back to X" buttons, back components such as `ContextBackButton`
  (and their imports), `router.back()` and `history.back()` calls;
- rename a back button for a step or panel inside a page to what it does
  ("Previous step") or where it goes ("Dashboard"), without the back arrow.
  An embedded frame's own Back and Forward, such as a preview browser's, stay;
- delete redirects from a settings or section landing page to its first child.
  A settings page is a list-detail page (`ShellListDetail`): on wide windows the
  list stays beside the open section, and on narrow ones the list is the
  landing page. Its `index.vue`, if it keeps one, is the empty detail
  placeholder;
- move a scroll behaviour the app sets through its own `createRouter` wrapper
  into `createShellRouter`'s `scrollBehavior` option, calling
  `shellScrollBehavior` for what it leaves to the shell: a wrapper that
  replaces the shell's throws at startup, since it would lose the position Up
  returns to. A hash target already opens below its `scroll-margin-top`.

## 6. Page actions go in the app bar

A page's own actions (Save, Edit, Delete, Refresh) move from rows of buttons in
the content into the app bar:

```vue
<ShellPageActions>
  <ShellPageAction icon="$edit" label="Edit" :to="editPath" />
  <ShellPageAction primary label="Save" @click="save" />
</ShellPageActions>
```

At most one action is `primary`; on compact windows the others show as icon
buttons named by their label.

A layout that draws its own top app bar instead of `ShellLayout` keeps it and
builds the page's part from the shell's pieces, so Up, the title and the
actions behave as in `ShellLayout`:

```vue
<script setup>
import { ShellPageActionsTarget, ShellPageTitle, ShellUpButton, useShellAppBar } from "@jskit-ai/shell-web/client";

useShellAppBar();
</script>

<template>
  <v-app-bar>
    <ShellUpButton />
    <ShellPageTitle title="Workspace" />
    <ShellPageActionsTarget />
    <!-- the app's own controls -->
  </v-app-bar>
  <v-main><slot /></v-main>
</template>
```

Delete the bar's own back button and the pages' own `h1`s: `ShellPageTitle` is
the page's one `h1`, and `jskit check` now counts the layout as a shell layout,
so its inner pages need parents.

## 7. CRUD screens

The CRUD screens apply all of this themselves. An app that customized them
changes:

- **List.** The create action is an extended FAB on compact and medium windows
  and the app bar's primary action on wider ones. Cards and table rows open the
  record when tapped; their overflow menu holds the other record actions. A
  table row's Open is a trailing chevron. Cards no longer show the record's id;
  a list shows names and figures, never ids.
  `CrudListRecordActionMenu` takes a `title` (the record's title, for its
  accessible name) instead of `buttonLabel`, `buttonVariant` and `buttonSize`.
  Filters are one chip row; the Filters chip opens every control in a bottom
  sheet (compact) or a dialog.
- **View.** Drop `resource-plural-title` from `CrudViewScreen`. Its `fields`
  slot is a list of value-first items:

  ```vue
  <template #fields="{ view }">
    <v-list-item :title="view.record?.author" subtitle="Author" />
  </template>
  ```

- **New and edit.** Cancel and Save are in the app bar. Save, Cancel and delete
  replace the form's history entry, so Back no longer reopens a finished form.
  `useCrudDeleteAction()` no longer takes a `router` option.
- **Translations.** `jskit.http.actions.actions` and `jskit.http.crud.view.backTo`
  are gone; `jskit.http.crud.list.recordActions` ("Actions for {title}") and
  `jskit.shell.actions.back` are new.

## 8. The navigation drawer and app tests

The drawer is 360dp wide; `drawerWidth="content"` on `ShellLayout` sizes it to
its items instead. Medium windows show the navigation rail, whose menu control
opens the drawer over the page. A modal drawer opens over the app bar, as
Material 3 draws it, so a browser test that clicked the menu control again to
close it taps the scrim or presses Escape instead.

Each main-navigation placement is literal data, one `addPlacement({ ... })`
per destination with plain string `surface` and suffixes; one a helper builds is
a `nav/placement-data` finding, and no page is judged for a missing parent until
it is declared literally.

## 9. Check it

Look at every screen at 390, 768 and 1280 pixels wide, in light and dark. A
change that needs app CSS to look right is a JSKIT default to report, not a
rule to add.
